Telling one group not to look at the other spoke to the daily, physical layout of the town.
studies.didYouKnow: The ayah before this one refers to seven repeated verses. Most early scholars take that to mean the opening surah, recited in every unit of prayer. Setting it beside the wealth of opponents compares two kinds of holding. That is done on purpose. The wing image turns up twice more in the Quran. It is used once about followers and once about ageing parents.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Envy is treated as a problem of attention before it is a problem of wanting. That is why the instruction is about the eyes. The passage also pulls apart two griefs that often run together. Sorrow at another person's refusal of guidance is real, and it is still set aside. The answer they give is not his to carry. What is left after both bans is not giving up. It is a turn. The last clause gives the freed attention somewhere to go.

crossReferences.why: Repeats the instruction almost exactly, adding that your Lord's provision is better and more lasting.
Gives the same command about lowering the wing, there over those who follow.
Tells the Prophet to stay with those who call on their Lord and not to look past them.

studies.applyIt: Notice the next time your eyes stay on someone else's life for longer than a glance: a photo, a car, a house someone posted. Do not argue with yourself about it. Just close the app or look away, and then do one small thing for a person who is actually near you. The ayah puts those two moves side by side for a reason.
studies.explainEasier: God tells the Prophet not to stare at the nice things other people have been given. He also tells him not to be sad about them. Instead he should be gentle and kind with the people who believe.

studies.title: Those Who Made It Pieces
studies.meaning: A short statement of role comes first. Then a warning drawn from an earlier case, and then the group it fits. Early scholars read the dividers in two main ways. Some take them as people who split scripture, keeping part and refusing part. Others follow a well-known report about men who split the roads into Mecca between them in the pilgrimage season, to turn arrivals away. The next word, for what was done to the recitation, means portions torn apart. The passage ends with an oath that everyone will be questioned.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, and from a season when visitors were arriving for the pilgrimage. The classical sources describe a planned effort to meet travellers on the roads into the valley. Different men were given different approaches, and each warned arrivals off before they could hear anything. The reports differ in detail. Early scholars cite them beside the reading about splitting scripture itself.

keyTerms.note: The second word means both plain in itself and making things plain. The role claimed is limited and precise: to state the matter clearly, which leaves the outcome entirely with the listener.
Occurring once in the Quran, from the root for dividing shares. It fits both readings, people apportioning scripture and men apportioning the roads into a city between themselves.
Also occurring once, linked by early Arabic dictionary writers to limbs pulled apart or a flock scattered. It describes something whole broken into fragments that can then be dismissed one at a time.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: The pilgrimage season brought tribes into the valley from across the peninsula. It was the one time of year when a message could reach beyond the city. Meeting arrivals on the approach roads was an effective answer to that. A traveller warned at the last well arrived ready to brush off what he heard. Control of the roads was control of the audience.
studies.didYouKnow: Both of the striking words in this passage occur only here in the whole Quran. One names the dividers. The other names what they made of the recitation. The Quran records a different complaint elsewhere about how this Book was treated. There the Messenger tells his Lord that his people left it alone, an image of desertion rather than of tearing apart.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Splitting a thing is shown here as a way of draining its force. A message taken whole has to be accepted or refused. A message broken into pieces can be handled piece by piece, and each piece answered on its own. That works on scripture, and it works on hearing too. The oath that closes the passage answers it. The questioning will cover everything a person did, taken together rather than piece by piece.

crossReferences.why: Records the other complaint about this Book, that his own people abandoned it entirely.
Gives the same role in its earliest form, the command to arise and warn.
States the questioning this oath promises, of the peoples sent to and of the messengers alike.

studies.applyIt: Notice whether you take the Quran in pieces you already agree with. Most of us have a working set: the verses that console, the ones that back our views. This week read a whole surah from start to end. Include the parts you usually pass over, and let it stand as one thing.
studies.explainEasier: Some people broke the Quran up into bits so they could brush each bit aside. Others stood on the roads into Mecca to warn visitors off before they heard it. God swears that every one of them will be asked what they did.

studies.title: We Suffice You Against Them
studies.meaning: An order to speak out is paired with an order to turn away. Both are given at once. Then comes a promise about the mockers. Then something rarer: God says the words are landing. We know your chest tightens at what they say. What is prescribed is not argument, and not silent endurance. It is praise and prostration. Early scholars note the point. What is offered for a social wound is a bodily act of worship, not a change of feeling.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan. The classical sources tie this instruction to the start of open public preaching, after a stretch when the message had spread more quietly. They differ over how long that earlier stretch lasted. Mockery from the leading families is well attested for these years. The Quran takes it up again and again in surahs from this time.

keyTerms.note: The verb for cleaving something so it separates, used of dawn breaking and of glass cracking. Applied to speech it means saying a thing so plainly that the matter divides around it.
A physical description of distress rather than a metaphor for sadness. The Quran locates the pressure of hostility in the body, which is why the remedy offered is also something done with the body.
The participle names a group rather than the act, so the instruction is to be among them. Belonging is prescribed alongside the posture, which matters for someone whose community had turned on him.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Ridicule had real force in a society built on honour. A mocking poem could damage a man's standing across the peninsula. Being laughed at in the assembly cost more than being argued with. Mockers were not a nuisance in that setting. They were doing something that worked, and everyone watching knew what it cost the man they were aimed at.
studies.didYouKnow: The Quran addresses this particular pressure more than once and always joins the remedy to praise. One passage tells him to endure what they say and to glorify his Lord before sunrise and before sunset. Another says he is before God's eyes and tells him to proclaim his Lord's praises when he rises. A short surah addressed to him opens by asking whether his chest was not expanded.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The distress is admitted rather than corrected, which is unusual. Nothing here tells him he should not feel the pressure. Nothing says the mockery does not matter. The instruction moves instead to something he can do, and it is bodily and repeatable. That treats a wounded state as something worked through by action, not settled by argument. The relief is placed in worship rather than in being proved right.

crossReferences.why: Joins the same instruction to endure what they say with praise before sunrise and sunset.
Names the same tightening of the chest and connects it to their demands for a treasure or an angel.
Opens by asking whether his chest was not expanded, and pairs hardship with ease twice.

studies.applyIt: The next time criticism lands and stays with you, do not reason with it. Do something physical and prescribed instead: pray two units, walk a fixed distance, read a page aloud. The remedy in this passage is an action rather than a thought, and it works on the state rather than on the argument.
studies.explainEasier: Say out loud what you were told to say, and let the people who laugh go. God says he knows their words hurt you. When they do, praise him and bow down with the others who bow.

studies.title: Until The Certainty Comes
studies.meaning: Nine words in Arabic close the surah, and everything turns on the last one. The particle before it means until. So worship is given a length of time, not a goal to reach. The classical scholars almost all read the certainty as death. Another surah backs that reading. It quotes people in the Fire who say they denied the Day of Judgement until the certainty came to them. Scholars use this verse to rule out laying devotion down once some inner state has been reached.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, and the last verse of the surah. Before it come an order to proclaim openly, a guarantee against the mockers, and word that the hostility is tightening his chest. Then praise and prostration are prescribed. This closing line stretches that prescription across a lifetime, not just across the present trouble. That is why it reads as a conclusion rather than an addition.

keyTerms.note: From a root for a servant bound to a master, so the word covers a whole standing relationship rather than particular acts. It is the same root behind the statement that jinn and human beings were made for this.
A particle of limit that marks an endpoint rather than a purpose. The distinction matters, since the sentence sets a duration for the instruction rather than naming a state to be reached by it.
Occurring six times in the Quran. Early scholars take it here as death, and another passage puts the same word in the mouths of people who denied the Judgement until it came upon them.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Duties in that world ended at points you could see. A debt closed on its date. A truce ran to the end of a sacred month. A contract of hire finished when the work was done. Everyone was used to duties with a stated edge. This instruction gives one too. But it sits at a point nobody can see coming and nobody can decline to reach.
studies.didYouKnow: The word that closes this surah occurs six times in the Quran. One passage uses it twice within three verses. It separates knowing a thing with certainty from seeing it with the eye of certainty. Another surah has the people of the Fire say they denied the Day of Judgement until the certainty came to them. That is the use the scholars lean on here.
studies.theologicalSignificance: Worship is marked by how long it lasts, not by what it achieves. That shuts one door. If the endpoint is death, no gain along the way lets anyone off, and no state of soul puts a person past the practice. It also makes the whole instruction one continuous thing rather than a run of episodes. The surah has spent its length on rejection, ruin and mockery. It ends by giving the reader one thing to keep doing.

crossReferences.why: Uses the same word in the mouths of the condemned, who denied the Judgement until it came.
Has a prophet describe prayer and charity enjoined on him for as long as he lives.
States the purpose this instruction assumes, that jinn and human beings were made to worship.

studies.applyIt: Pick the smallest act of worship you can commit to every single day without exception. Two units of prayer, one page, one repeated phrase. Make it small enough that no bad week can break it. The verse sets a duration rather than a target, and something durable is worth more here than something impressive.
studies.explainEasier: Keep serving your Lord until the sure thing comes. Almost all the old readers took that to mean until you die. There is no point along the way where you have done enough and can stop.
